title: Sugarbush South planning and Labrador Drive purchase
subtitle: Also: first look at a 30-storey Albert Street tower proposal and a notice of motion on US tariffs.
overview: Council directed staff to hire a consultant to prepare a land use plan and planning framework for Sugarbush South, part of work to enable medium-rise housing in the neighbourhood {{vote:m2}}. Council also approved the City's purchase of the Labrador Drive extension and Campus Drive, and directed that they be established as public highways {{vote:m3}}. The highway by-law was passed later in the meeting.

Council held an informal public meeting on a proposed 30-storey tower with 230 units at 177-179 Albert Street. No decision was made. Staff will review the application and report back, and a formal public meeting will be held later. A resident spoke against the proposal, citing neighbourhood character, traffic and heritage concerns.

The Mayor tabled a notice of motion on proposed US tariffs, for consideration on February 24. It would ask the Waterloo Economic Development Corporation for an action plan to support local businesses and direct staff to review City procurement for Canadian sources. Councillors also shared community news, including neighbourhood events and active bystander training.

decisions.detail: Council received report IPPW2025-001 and directed staff to retain a consultant to prepare a comprehensive land use plan and planning framework for Sugarbush South.

Council approved report CORP2025-001 and authorized the Mayor, Clerk and/or City Solicitor to sign the agreements needed to buy the Labrador Drive extension and Campus Drive, including municipal services and easements.
Council directed that a by-law be enacted to establish the Labrador Drive extension and Campus Drive as public highways.

debate: On Sugarbush South, one councillor asked about parkland and green space. Staff said parkland acquisition is handled by City staff, with a future capital project planned, and that the consultant's work focuses on official plan and zoning policies.

Another councillor asked whether Sugarbush South could be linked to other green spaces so they are not isolated. Staff said walkways have been identified, noting the area's proximity to two LRT stations, and that a future official plan amendment will likely include a map of desired walkways.

On the Albert Street proposal, councillors asked about the transition to the neighbouring Heritage Conservation District. Staff said shadow, wind, setbacks and podium step-backs will be considered in their review and that they would follow up on why the zoning boundaries were drawn as they were.

The applicant's team said the site is near transit and the university, and that the proposal fits the direction of the newer official plan update. They said the tower is slender, and that they are offering affordable units voluntarily. Councillors asked why the affordable units were included when they are not required.

A resident delegate opposed the amendment, citing traffic, parking, garbage, groundwater, wind, shadow and effects on the adjacent heritage neighbourhood. The delegate said the community could accept a building of about 8 to 12 storeys and suggested considering nearby properties for a better site design.
